title: how to wire a new query command to both CLI and MCP surfaces
summary: To add a new query command (e.g., `trace`), implement a shared engine returning {__rawText} that both CLI and MCP call through thin wrappers. The pattern: CLI registration in main() → parse args → load cache → call shared engine → emit __rawText; MCP registration in TOOL_DEFINITIONS + CallToolRequestSchema → parse params → call shared engine → wrap __rawText in MCP response. This ensures identical results on both surfaces from one implementation.

steps.role: CLI wrapper: parseQueryArgs, load cache, call shared engine, print __rawText
MCP adapter: calls shared engines, wraps __rawText in response object
MCP registration: tool schema definition and CallToolRequestSchema case handler
entry dispatch: subcommand check for CLI, cache reader factory for MCP

invariants: Every query command's shared engine returns {__rawText: string} with optional {error: string}
CLI: emit __rawText directly to stdout; MCP: wrap unchanged in content[0].text
Cache loading: getIndex (CLI, per-query) vs makeCacheReader (MCP, long-lived with mtime polling)
